thread:
incident-bot: INCIDENT: High 5xx/error rate detected for apac region via Provider-Blue — auto-page sent to #incidents :rotating_light:

irod (oncall): I'm on it. seeing spike ~18:23 UTC in apac-edge-1 -> provider-blue. errors are mostly 502/503 on decode/tokenization. Dashboard: https://status.redwood.ai/insights/17895

irod (oncall): immediate mitigation plan: 1) soft-rate-limit at edge for anonymous/low-tier traffic 2) route 35% of non-SLA traffic to provider-green (eu fallback) 3) start draining apac worker pool for provider-blue 4) notify support for customers >1% error

raj: acked. I'll run the traffic commands. doing a quick smoke: `redwoodctl health check --region apac --provider blue` returns intermittent timeouts.

omar: logs show increased backend latency hitting provider-blue's inference nodes, KV cache miss rate up ~2x. suspect provider-side load-shed.

lina: support-runbook step: prepare a short message for impacted customers and mark top-10 as P1 for targeted outreach. maria, can you start drafting?

maria: on it. drafting now. Will post to status.redwood.ai once we confirm mitigations.

raj: applying soft rate limit for anonymous tier:```bash
redwoodctl traffic limit apply --region apac --provider blue --policy soft --match "tier:anonymous" --qps 4
```

raj: also configuring route shift for non-SLA traffic to provider-green:```bash
redwoodctl traffic shift --from provider:blue --to provider:green --region apac --percent 35 --filter "!sla:enterprise"
```

irod (oncall): good. please keep enterprise customers pinned to provider-blue for now (we need stronger guarantees). raj, can you add an emergency retry/backoff policy at the client-proxy?

raj: done. added `retry:3 backoff:200ms max_backoff:2s` at the edge for apac. Also increased circuit-breaker threshold to avoid cascading failures.

omar: starting to drain apac worker pool for provider-blue (scale-down incoming connections) — command: `kubectl annotate svc apac-blue-drain=initiated --overwrite` and `redwoodctl pool drain --region apac --provider blue --grace 120`

ada (product): any feature-level brownouts we should consider? realtime-metadata and on-the-fly language detection are noisy — could disable them for non-enterprise to reduce per-request work.

irod (oncall): yes, partial brownout: disable language-detect and realtime-metadata for free/prodtrial customers only. keep enterprise unchanged.

lina: support note: impacted endpoints - /v1/generate, /v1/embeddings. Top affected customers: Acme (0.9% overall traffic but 6.2% error rate), BlinkHealth (2.1% traffic, 8% error), internal: playground sessions spiking. Will prepare targeted pings.

maria: posted initial status page: "Investigating increased errors in APAC affecting some customers; mitigation in progress. Partial routing to secondary provider in effect." Added contact for enterprise customers. :white_check_mark:

raj: telemetry update: after shift to provider-green + soft rate limit, error rate dropped from 18% -> 6% in last 4m. Latency median also improved ~120ms -> 85ms for routed traffic. Still seeing spikes on provider-blue fallback attempts.

irod (oncall): continuing to monitor. next steps: keep route at 35% for 15m, then increase to 50% if stable. keep drain in place until provider-blue confirms capacity. Also create degradations list for features to be rolled back if things worsen.

omar: provider-blue contacted via provider-ops channel; they report an internal autoscaler lag. ETA unknown. Meanwhile our fallback looks stable.

ada (product): support message approved, will prep template for customers with high error volume.

irod (oncall): NOTE -> Handoff planned at 19:00 UTC to raj for continued mitigation. I'll leave detailed notes in the incident doc. tagging @raj for takeover.

raj: taking over at 19:00 UTC. Checklist on takeover: 1) confirm route % 2) watch enterprise tail errors 3) readiness to increase to 50% 4) ensure no regressions in QA traffic.

maria: support outreach sent to Acme & BlinkHealth (DMs + incident channel). asked for logs and recent request IDs.

raj: increasing route to 50% for non-enterprise after stability window: `redwoodctl traffic shift --from provider:blue --to provider:green --region apac --percent 50 --filter "!sla:enterprise"`

raj: also applied quota bump for enterprise customers to avoid throttling: `redwoodctl quota set --customer Acme --region apac --qps 40` (temporary)

omar: monitoring: error rate now ~2.1% region-wide, enterprise error rate under 0.5%. CPU usage on provider-blue nodes slowly decreasing as we drain.

irod (oncall): great. plan to keep partial brownouts in place until provider-blue confirms full recovery and we've validated tail latencies for 1hr.

maria: support note updated with 'partial brownout & provider reroute in effect; enterprise customers unaffected in general' and links to ask for logs.

ada (product): marking impacted feature flags: `lang-detect:false for free` and `realtime-meta:false for free` — make sure these are reversible.

raj: rolling back language-detect brownout for enterprise only: `featurectl set lang-detect --customers enterprise --state enabled` (explicit). Free-tier remains off.

incident-bot: Incident timeline updated: incident start 1789504321, current mitigations applied: soft-rate-limit, 50% reroute to provider-green for non-enterprise, partial brownout of non-critical features for free tier, enterprise quotas preserved.

irod (oncall): decision: start slow re-introduce to provider-blue at 19:45 UTC by reducing reroute to 30% and monitor. If error rate stays <1% for 20m, continue reduce.

raj: reduced reroute to 30%. Observing for 25m. Will keep enterprise pinned.

omar: metrics look stable. provider-blue still shows higher latencies but within acceptable bounds for retried traffic.

maria: prepping final incident message for customers with timeline and mitigations. Also flags for post-incident: clearer SLA-grade routing rules and automated fallback tie-breakers.

irod (oncall): handing back to raj for final validation and postmortem prep. I'll start the incident template: gather logs, reaction timeline, and customer impact table.

raj: will own postmortem and follow up with provider to understand autoscaler lag. Will also schedule a runbook update to add a forced quicker reroute option and an automated brownout toggle in Console.

ada (product): noted. product will propose a conservative feature-degradation matrix for next oncall runbook.

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED (provisional): traffic normalized and user-visible errors reduced to baseline. Final resolution pending provider postmortem and our follow-up. :tada:

irod (oncall): thanks team. Great coordination. Follow-up items: 1) postmortem by raj 2) runbook update 3) customer communication complete 4) provider deep-dive. Closing handover at 20:12 UTC.

raj: acknowledged. I'll drop the postmortem link when ready and include commands we ran, diff of traffic rules, and recommendations.

maria: support closing messages queued and sent. Will follow-up with customers who reported errors.

ada (product): adding incident to roadmap for automated reroute and brownout playbooks.

irod (oncall): closing thread. Good job everyone. :thumbsup:
